concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation, along with the presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG, are consistent with autoimmune encephalitis.

The patient's symptoms of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation, along with the presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG, are consistent with Hashimoto encephalopathy.

The patient's symptoms of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation, along with the presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG, are consistent with limbic encephalitis.

The patient's symptoms of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation, along with the presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG, are consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.

The patient's symptoms of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation, along with the presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG, are consistent with subacute sclerosing panencephalitis.

The patient's symptoms of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation, along with the presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG, are consistent with Rasmussen encephalitis.

rationales.F01: Abnormal behavior is a common symptom of autoimmune encephalitis.
rationales.F06: Confusion, impaired attention, and disorientation are common symptoms of autoimmune encephalitis.
rationales.F08: Myoclonic jerks are a common symptom of autoimmune encephalitis and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.
rationales.F11: Generalized background slowing on EEG is a common finding in autoimmune encephalitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of abnormal behavior, decreased concentration, postural instability, and confusion, along with the lack of response to antivirals and antibiotics, and the subsequent empirical treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin, supports the diagnosis of Autoimmune Encephalitis. The presence of myoclonic jerks and generalized background slowing on EEG also aligns with this diagnosis, although Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease is also considered due to these features.
